correctness.rationale: Löwner feasibility Z<=A<=KZ is symmetrized over S_(n-1); this proves reduction from all positive diagonal scalings to two-level factors. The two-dimensional block has determinant x²(1+t(a²+kb²)) and det(B-I)=tkb²(x²-1). For x<=1, minimizing λ+/λ- reduces by the trace/determinant invariant to minimizing Px+Q/x; for x>=1 the largest eigenvalue increases strictly. The exact threshold and formulas follow. Standard-library numerical checker verifies 2310 sampled comparisons; this does not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: The one-spike SPD family is a standard positive-definite covariance/Hessian benchmark with diagonal preconditioning. The mass threshold exactly decides when any per-coordinate rescaling can improve condition number, not merely whether a particular heuristic helps. All diagonal factors, including symmetry-breaking ones, are covered. The explicit n=5 case shows a substantive practical divergence: Jacobi equilibration worsens the condition number beyond the no-scaling baseline while an optimal scaling improves it. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary finite parameter value.
